All three unwraps sit in router.rs, so the fix (swap `.unwrap()` for `?` and append `# Ok::<(), harw_web::error::WebError>(())` to each of the three doctest blocks) is fully contained in that one file.

title: Execute path silently runs with an unscoped OpContext if no resolved identity is present
description: When no ResolvedPeer is present, the Execute branch passes the factory context through unchanged: tenant None, which tenant_admits treats as seeing all tenants. Today that branch cannot be reached, because decide_resolved_route only returns Execute when identity is Some. But the fallback is the wrong way round: a refactor of the decision path (for example calling decide_route instead) would run operations unscoped instead of refusing. R15 rule M1: fallbacks must refuse.
evidence: server.rs:714-720 `let ctx = (context_factory)(&peer, caller_tier); let ctx = match resolved { Some(resolved) => resolved.scope_op_context(ctx), None => ctx, };`; harw-operations/src/context.rs:415-418 `match scope { None => true, ... }`
fix: Before building ctx and reading the body: `let Some(resolved) = resolved else { return Ok(forbidden_response(forbidden_reason_str(ForbiddenReason::UnknownPeer))); };`, then `resolved.scope_op_context(ctx)` with no Option. A stronger alternative is to let RouteDecision::Execute carry the &ResolvedPeer (router.rs), which makes the None case unrepresentable.
test_idea: Extract `fn scoped_context(resolved: Option<&ResolvedPeer>, ctx: OpContext) -> Result<OpContext, WebResponse>` and assert None yields a 403 response. Central build: cargo test -p harw-web.
reasons:
Confirmed against the current working tree; evidence holds exactly as cited.

harw-web/src/server.rs:709-720 (Execute arm of `handle`):
```
RouteDecision::Execute { route, caller_tier } => {
    ...
    let ctx = (context_factory)(&peer, caller_tier);
    let ctx = match resolved {
        Some(resolved) => resolved.scope_op_context(ctx),
        None => ctx,
    };
```
`resolved` is `Option<&ResolvedPeer>` computed independently of `decision` (server.rs:681-684), so nothing in the type system ties the `Execute` arm to `Some`.

harw-web/src/router.rs:250-297: `decide_resolved_route` calls the shared `decide_with_tier(..., || identity.map(ResolvedPeer::tier))` (router.rs:256). `decide_with_tier` returns `Forbidden{ UnknownPeer }` whenever `caller_tier()` is `None` (router.rs:277-281), and only reaches `RouteDecision::Execute` after that check passes (router.rs:293-296). So today `Execute` is provably only produced when `identity` (i.e. `resolved`) is `Some` — the `None` arm at server.rs:719 is dead code, matching the finding's own claim.

harw-operations/src/context.rs:415-418 confirms `tenant_admits(None, _) == true` — an unscoped `OpContext` (tenant `None`) is treated as admitting every tenant, exactly as cited.

Checked for anything that would make this a non-issue: `decide_route` (the non-identity-resolved variant) is never called from production code — only from doctests/unit tests in router.rs and harw-web/tests/method_admission.rs (verified via grep). So `handle()` in server.rs is the sole production caller, and it only ever calls `decide_resolved_route`, not `decide_route`. There is no compiler-enforced invariant (no `#[non_exhaustive]`/newtype) linking `RouteDecision::Execute` to a non-optional `ResolvedPeer`; the module doc at server.rs:61-63 documents the invariant in prose ("Bei `Execute` fädelt … Mandant … ein") but the code does not encode it, which is exactly the fail-open-fallback-on-refactor risk pattern M1 describes. The finding is honest that the branch is unreachable today (not an active exploit) and rates itself 'low' — this is accurate self-assessment, not an overclaim.

The primary proposed fix (early `let Some(resolved) = resolved else { return Ok(forbidden_response(...)); };` before line 714) touches only harw-web/src/server.rs. The "stronger alternative" (moving `&ResolvedPeer` into `RouteDecision::Execute` in router.rs) would span two files, but that is explicitly offered as an alternative, not the primary fix, and the finding itself states `single_file: true; other files: none`, which matches the primary fix.

No changes were made; this was a read-only verification. No cargo/rustc/build commands were run, per the binding build rule.

Confirmed by reading router.rs:250-297 (decide_resolved_route -> decide_with_tier) that RouteDecision::Execute can only be returned when caller_tier() is Some, which for decide_resolved_route requires identity (the `resolved` arg) to be Some (router.rs:256, 277-281). So the `None => ctx` arm at server.rs:719 is unreachable today, exactly as the finding itself admits. The invariant is handled elsewhere: decide_with_tier is the single gate shared by both decide_route and decide_resolved_route, and its contract is documented at router.rs:220-236 ('Execute' implies scope_op_context is 'der einzige Weg, auf dem ein Mandant in eine Operation gelangt'). Additionally, even the hypothetical fallback effect (unscoped context sees all tenants) is itself deliberate, pre-existing, documented behavior for single-user mode (harw-operations/src/context.rs:393-401, 'Einzelnutzer-Betrieb ... das bisherige Verhalten bleibt unverändert'; masterplan H12 section), not a newly introduced silent bypass. The migration ledger (MIG-013/MIG-014) shows tenant scoping into OpContext as landed and tracks tenant-filtering gaps elsewhere, never flagging this hand-off. This is a redundant defensive branch guarded by an already-enforced and documented invariant one layer up, not a live authz gap — a legitimate but purely speculative refactor-safety suggestion (make Execute carry &ResolvedPeer to make None unrepresentable), which the finding's own text concedes cannot be reached today.

Confirmed by reading the code. harw-web/src/router.rs:250-297 (decide_resolved_route -> decide_with_tier) shows caller_tier() is `identity.map(ResolvedPeer::tier)`, so RouteDecision::Execute is only returned when identity/`resolved` is Some(_) -- the None arm at harw-web/src/server.rs:717-720 is unreachable today, exactly as the finding states. harw-operations/src/context.rs:415-419 confirms tenant_admits(None, _) = true (unscoped sees every tenant), so if that None arm were ever reached the OpContext would run unscoped -- a real fail-open fallback, matching the project's own documented M1 pattern (docs/planning/85-gap-hunt/R15-patterns.md: "Fallbacks must refuse"; MIG-013 in docs/planning/90-migration-ledger/MIGRATION_LEDGER.md notes tenant filtering is still being built out, so this invariant is live and load-bearing, not settled history). No decision doc in docs/planning/70-decisions or docs/guides addresses or excuses this fallback. The R15-patterns doc itself also warns (pattern P4) that intent-side dissent on this class of finding is usually "defense-in-depth, not an acute bug" -- consistent with the finding's own "low" severity label, so this is a real, correctly-scoped, non-style defect worth tracking, not an overstated claim.

Fixable in one file: yes. `handle` (server.rs:640) is a private fn called only once, from server.rs:500 -- no external callers. The minimal fix -- replacing the `match resolved { Some(r) => r.scope_op_context(ctx), None => ctx }` at server.rs:717-720 with an early `let Some(resolved) = resolved else { return Ok(forbidden_response(forbidden_reason_str(ForbiddenReason::UnknownPeer))); };` -- uses only items already in scope in server.rs (ForbiddenReason and forbidden_response are already used at server.rs:693-699; forbidden_reason_str is a private fn defined in the same file at server.rs:998). It requires no signature or type change to decide_resolved_route, RouteDecision, or ResolvedPeer, so no caller elsewhere breaks. The "stronger alternative" the finding also mentions (moving &ResolvedPeer into RouteDecision::Execute in router.rs) would span router.rs + server.rs, but that is offered only as an alternative, not the fix being evaluated; the primary proposed fix is single-file.

title: GET /events authorizes only at subscription: revoked or expired security contexts keep streaming, and there is no tenant filter
description: handle_events resolves the identity once and then streams indefinitely through a detached task. In security_hub mode a context has a TTL of at most 900 s and can be revoked (DELETE /v1/contexts/{id}), yet the SSE stream keeps delivering. The process-wide bus also carries every tenant's OperationCompleted events (operation name and outcome) to every subscriber, which bypasses the §15 tenant scoping applied to operation routes.
evidence: server.rs:831-834 `if let Err(error) = resolve_identity(identity, peer, headers).await { return forbidden_response(error.code()); } sse_response(Arc::clone(events))`; :850-866 detached `tokio::spawn(async move { loop { ... subscription.recv().await ... } })` with no re-check.
fix: Pass the ResolvedPeer into sse_response. If summary() is Some, end the stream at summary.expires_at (tokio::time::sleep_until in the select) and re-resolve on each heartbeat, closing the stream on failure. Once WebEventKind carries a tenant, filter OperationCompleted by it.
test_idea: Use a FakeHub resolver that returns Active and then Gone: subscribe, trigger a heartbeat, and assert that the body stream ends.
reasons:
CONFIRMED — the finding reproduces on the current working tree exactly as described.

Answer: real. Both sub-claims hold.

1) Authorization checked once, never re-checked for the life of the stream.
- `handle_events` (harw-web/src/server.rs:804-834) calls `resolve_identity(identity, peer, headers).await` at line 831 solely to gate entry: `if let Err(error) = resolve_identity(...).await { return forbidden_response(error.code()); }` (server.rs:831-833). The `Ok(ResolvedPeer)` value is discarded — never bound to a variable, never passed onward.
- Line 834 calls `sse_response(Arc::clone(events))` (server.rs:847), which takes only the event bus, no peer/identity/expiry argument at all.
- `sse_response` (server.rs:847-876) does `tokio::spawn(async move { loop { subscription.recv().await ... } })` (server.rs:850-866). The loop only ends on `WebEventReceiveError::Closed` (bus dropped) or a failed `send_data` (client TCP disconnect, server.rs:862-864). There is no timer, no re-resolution, no reference to `ResolvedPeer::summary()`/`expires_at` anywhere in this function or its caller.
- `ResolvedPeer::summary()` (harw-web/src/identity.rs:162-166) exposes `SecurityContextSummary` with `expires_at`; `SecurityHubResolver::resolve_inner` (identity.rs:520-593) is what enforces expiry/revocation (`summary.expires_at <= self.clock.now()` → `ContextGone`, identity.rs:560-561) and is exactly what's skipped after the initial check.
- Server-side TTL cap is confirmed at `harw-security-hub/src/policy.rs:56` (`DEFAULT_MAX_TTL_SECS: u64 = 900`) and revocation via `DELETE /v1/contexts/{id}` is confirmed at `harw-security-hub/src/server.rs:446` (`Method::DELETE => revoke_context(...)`) and :569-578, which flips future `GET /v1/contexts/{id}` verification to `410 Gone` (server.rs:564, "Lookup::Revoked"). None of that ever reaches a running `/events` connection. A background heartbeat exists (`server.rs:422-427,444-445`, `self.events.publish(WebEventKind::Heartbeat)`), but it is a process-wide keep-alive signal with no per-connection identity check — it does not substitute for re-authorization.
